anomaly_def.Name: Schema and Index Design Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Schema and Index Design Anomaly : Physical data-model, indexing, partitioning, or datatype choices are misaligned with workload access patterns, forcing inefficient execution paths independent of statistics or optimizer faults.
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly : Allocated data, index, log, or temp space approaches or reaches exhaustion, causing allocation failures, halted growth, and stalled background maintenance.

Composite definition: The database simultaneously suffers from sub-optimal schema/index design and imminent or actual exhaustion of critical storage areas. Poor data layout magnifies space consumption while also generating inefficient I/O patterns that accelerate space depletion, so application activity is constrained both by slow queries and by hard space limits.

Combined observable phenomena:  • Growing tables and non-covering or redundant indexes balloon disk usage, shrinking free space far faster than capacity planning assumes.  • Queries already performing full table or full index scans spill to on-disk sorts or hash areas, rapidly filling TEMP segments and triggering "out of space" errors.  • DML operations against poorly clustered or over-indexed tables hit "cannot allocate extent" or "autoextend failed" messages mid-transaction, causing rollbacks, lock retention, and user-visible timeouts.  • Emergency index rebuilds or partition maintenance meant to mitigate poor designs cannot complete because of insufficient work space, leaving bloated structures in place and worsening performance.  • Monitoring shows interleaved patterns of escalating latency and sudden statement failures related to space, making the root cause appear intermittent and multifaceted.

Causal interaction: Inefficient schema and indexing choices inflate row length, duplicate data in overlapping indexes, and prevent effective partition pruning; this amplifies data and index growth, quickly consuming tablespace, log, and temp capacity. As free space dwindles, the database's ability to allocate new extents, write redo/undo, or create temporary segments degrades, leading to frequent space errors that interrupt queries already slowed by poor access paths. Conversely, space pressure blocks corrective actions such as adding proper covering indexes, reorganizing tables, or implementing partitioning, locking the system into a feedback loop where design inefficiencies accelerate space exhaustion and space shortages prevent design remediation. The intertwined root causes thus reinforce each other, producing severe throughput collapse, elevated latency, and operational instability across both OLTP and analytical workloads.

entry.error_class: Class 42 - Syntax Error or Access Rule Violation
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with unsupported syntax, invalid statement structure, or feature usage that the target engine version cannot execute as written.
entry.solution_guidance: Validate SQL syntax, target-engine compatibility, statement shape, and whether the feature is supported under the current engine version or execution context.
